channel.title: Security Brief
channel.description: Original analysis and ranked cybersecurity news with links to original sources

item.title: The edge is where attackers get in: this week's firewall, VPN and remote-access exploits
item.description: Five exploited flaws in firewalls, VPNs, remote-support software and file-sharing servers show one pattern. The systems that sit at the edge of your network, and that administrators manage remotely, are the weakest link. Here is what to check first.

item.title: October 2026 Patch Tuesday: what the Microsoft feed shows and what to do
item.description: The Microsoft feed lists few entries, and most of them are updates to October's release rather than new fixes. The one item that needs planning is a .NET remote code execution flaw that Microsoft has not fixed yet. Identity Web and WSL need version checks if you use them.

item.title: Weekly M365 & Entra Briefing: 13 to 19 October 2026
item.description: Exchange sign-in problems after October Windows Server updates, an identity-based incident at ConnectWise that affected Microsoft 365 tenants, and why device-code abuse is still worth a Conditional Access check.

item.title: Recent UnrealIRCd Vulnerability Exploited in Attacks
item.description: Tracked as CVE-2026-114713, the high-severity flaw allows attackers to execute commands with server/IRCOp privileges. The post Recent UnrealIRCd Vulnerability Exploited in Attacks appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: MSP ScreenConnect Servers Targeted in Month-Long Campaign
item.description: More than 40 servers received over 688,000 requests exploiting CVE-2026-84869 to execute guest-pushed files. The post MSP ScreenConnect Servers Targeted in Month-Long Campaign appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.description: The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned on Tuesday that hackers are now exploiting a high-severity Cisco BroadWorks vulnerability in attacks.

item.title: November Patch Tuesday: An Overflowing Cornucopia of CVEs
item.description: Microsoft serves up an actively exploited Outlook zero-day, and a wave of critical Exchange, SharePoint, Windows Search, and LDAP bugs that exhausted defenders need to prioritize fast.

item.title: Uber notifies drivers of data breach affecting nearly 150,000 people
item.description: Ride-hailing company Uber is notifying nearly 150,000 drivers that attackers stole their data after breaching AI infrastructure provider Fireworks in early October.

item.title: Barracuda links cloud breach to ARTEX AI-powered cyberattack
item.description: Hackers who breached the cloud environment of network and email security company Barracuda earlier this month used a stolen cloud access key and the ARTEX AI penetration testing framework.

item.title: FBI warns ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering global cyberattacks
item.description: The FBI is warning that hackers are using an AI-powered penetration testing framework called ARTEX to automate cyberattacks against organizations worldwide, including a recent ConnectWise supply-chain breach that compromised Microsoft 365 customer environments.

item.title: Ransomware Attacks Increase Behind AI, But Payments Decline
item.description: Large language models and other AI systems allow a growing number of ransomware groups to create convincing phishing emails and identify sensitive data quickly.

item.title: Ransomware attack on Belarusian cloud firm disrupts businesses for days
item.description: ActiveCloud said hackers had breached its systems and encrypted parts of its cloud infrastructure, leaving customers unable to access key services for several days.

item.title: Kazakhstan-linked hackers used AI agent to spy on Central Asian governments
item.description: Suspected Kazakhstan-linked hackers used an artificial intelligence agent to help spy on Central Asian governments, steal sensitive documents and infiltrate critical infrastructure networks, according to new research.

item.title: Uber says nearly 150,000 impacted by third-party breach
item.description: In breach notification letters, the rideshare company said it was notified by a third party service provider on October 9 that internal credentials were stolen and used to access Uber’s account.
